title: Orsen and the Gravity
premise: Lena Ishikawa, an insurance investigator who has spent ten years cataloguing impossible accidents in contested orbits, is assigned to the Meridian, a cargo ship returned from deep space with a crew aged backward by decades and no memory of how. Hidden in the ship's quantum core is a message from a long-lost colony that proves the war's founding atrocity was staged by the Coalition itself — evidence that could end the war or shatter the last fragile peace. Pursued by both fleets and betrayed by the woman he loves, Coalition officer Mara Voss, Lena must choose between delivering the truth and protecting the people who trust him. In the end he broadcasts the message to every ship in the system at the cost of his own freedom, and the war ends not with victory but with both fleets refusing to fight a lie anymore.
about_author: O. M. Blackwood is a former maritime insurance adjuster who turned to science fiction after a career spent investigating losses at sea. Writing from a coastal town whose name they decline to share, Blackwood specializes in stories about ordinary professionals caught in extraordinary moral weather.

chapters.title: Actuarial
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Investigating a cargo pod that vanished inside a shielded lane, Lena establishes his world: ten years of impossible accidents, a war fought over shipping lanes no one remembers starting. The pod reappears containing a message addressed to him by name. Beat: restless competence cracking into dread.

chapters.title: The Meridian Comes Home
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The Meridian docks after eleven years missing, its crew aged backward — a navigator now a teenager, the captain a young man again. Lena is the only investigator both fleets will accept as neutral. He boards alone. Beat: uncanny wonder shadowed by grief for a crew that lost a decade of living.

chapters.title: Younger Every Hour
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, intercut with the young captain's fragmented memories. The reversal is ongoing; the crew is forgetting their voyage as their brains restructure. Lena finds the quantum core sealed with his own authorization codes from a future he hasn't lived. Beat: intimacy with people who are becoming strangers to themselves.

chapters.title: Voss
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Coalition officer Mara Voss boards under a diplomatic flag — his former lover, ten years estranged, now tasked with seizing the ship. Their negotiation is a duel of old wounds and mutual respect. She warns him the Coalition will burn the Meridian rather than let it dock. Beat: love rekindled against better judgment.

chapters.title: The Staged Atrocity
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Cracking the core, he finds the message: sensor records proving the Kaltera Station massacre that started the war was committed by Coalition black-ops, not the Outer Belt factions. The colony that recorded it was erased. Beat: the vertigo of justice outside the law — every side he's served built on a lie.

chapters.title: What the Crew Gave Up
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: the young navigator, Toma, remembers enough to tell Lena the crew chose the reversal deliberately, spending their years as the price of carrying the message home. They knew no one would believe the living, so they became evidence themselves. Beat: sacrifice as testimony; Lena's resolve hardens into duty.

chapters.title: Interdiction
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Both fleets converge on the Meridian in the gravity well of a dead moon. Mara offers him extraction and a quiet life if he surrenders the core; he refuses. She lets him go anyway, and is arrested for it. Beat: love against duty made literal — she chooses him over her uniform and pays for it.

chapters.title: The Long Fall
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, with Toma's POV in the escape. Fleeing in a courier with the core, Lena runs the blockade through the debris fields where he built his career. Toma, now nearly a child, is forgetting the message's meaning even as they carry it. Beat: a chase that is also a countdown — memory and time both running out.

chapters.title: Gravity
chapters.summary: Climax. Lena's POV. Cornered above the war's oldest battlefield, Lena realizes a private delivery will be buried, so he slingshots into the system's shared relay and broadcasts the message — the massacre, the erased colony, the crew's testimony — to every ship, both fleets. The Meridian's sacrifice becomes public truth. Beat: terrible clarity; he surrenders himself as the data spreads.

chapters.title: After the Silence
chapters.summary: Resolution, Mara's POV then Lena's. Fleets refuse engagement; tribunals begin; Mara, released, testifies. Lena, imprisoned for the broadcast, receives a pardon petition signed by both fleets' crews — and a visit from Toma, who remembers nothing but came anyway. Beat: belonging found not in nations but in the people who choose you; justice begun, war ended.
